title: Neuro-Ophthalmic Mastery: The Pupil & Multiple Sclerosis
summary: A high-yield clinical roadmap for the evaluation of Relative Afferent Pupillary Defects (RAPD) and the comprehensive management of Multiple Sclerosis. Designed for residents and fellows focusing on textbook-level diagnostics and landmark trial evidence.

branches: Afferent: Retinal Ganglion Cells -> Optic Nerve -> Chiasm -> Optic Tract
Pretectal: Fibers exit tract before LGN -> Pretectal Nuclei (Midbrain)
Interneuron: Pretectal nuclei to bilateral Edinger-Westphal (EW) Nuclei
Efferent: EW Nucleus -> CN III -> Ciliary Ganglion -> Short Ciliary Nerves -> Sphincter Pupillae

sections.title: Defining the RAPD (Marcus Gunn Pupil)
sections.content: A Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD) occurs when there is an asymmetric response to a light stimulus between the two eyes. It indicates a lesion in the pre-chiasmal afferent pathway (optic nerve or severe retinal disease). Note: A dense cataract does NOT cause an RAPD.

sections.title: The Swinging Flashlight Test Protocol
content: 1. Dim room lighting; patient fixes on a distant target to negate accommodation.
2. Use a bright, focal light source (transilluminator).
3. Shine light in Eye A for 2-3 seconds, then quickly swing to Eye B.
4. Observe the initial movement of the pupil in Eye B.
5. Repeat the swing rhythmically to confirm the 'escape' or dilation.

rows: Weak initial constriction followed by greater escape/redilation.
Initial stall/no movement followed by immediate dilation.
No response in the affected eye; consensual only in the fellow eye.

branches: Optic Nerve: Optic Neuritis (MS), NAION, AION (GCA), Glaucoma (asymmetric), Trauma, Compression
Retinal: Massive Retinal Detachment, Ischemic CRVO, Severe Macular Degeneration (extensive)
Pre-Chiasmal: Optic Tract lesions (contralateral RAPD), Chiasmal compression (asymmetric)

sections.title: 2017 McDonald Criteria for MS
content: Dissemination in Space (DIS): ≥1 T2-hyperintense lesion in ≥2 of 4 MS-typical CNS areas (Periventricular, Cortical/Juxtacortical, Infratentorial, Spinal Cord).
Dissemination in Time (DIT): Simultaneous presence of gadolinium-enhancing and non-enhancing lesions OR a new T2/Gd+ lesion on follow-up.
CSF Oligoclonal Bands: Can substitute for DIT in some cases.
No better clinical explanation for the neurological deficits.

sections.title: Ocular Manifestations of MS
content: Optic Neuritis: Pain with eye movement (92%), sudden vision loss, dyschromatopsia (red desaturation).
Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia (INO): Lesion in MLF; ipsilateral adduction deficit, contralateral abducting nystagmus.
Intermediate Uveitis: Pars planitis and 'snowbanking' are significantly associated with MS.
Periphlebitis Retinae: Venous sheathing found in up to 10% of cases.
Nystagmus: Pendular or jerk nystagmus (often vestibular or cerebellar involvement).

sections.title: Acute Treatment of Optic Neuritis (ONTT Protocol)
content: Step 1: IV Methylprednisolone (1,000 mg/day) for 3 days.
Step 2: Follow with Oral Prednisone (1 mg/kg/day) for 11 days.
Step 3: Rapid taper over 3-4 days (e.g., 20mg day 1, 10mg day 2/3).
CONTRAINDICATION: Do NOT use low-dose oral steroids alone (increased recurrence rate per Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial).

rows: First-line for RRMS; high safety profile, modest efficacy.
Fingolimod requires monitoring for FAME (Fingolimod Associated Macular Edema).
High efficacy. Natalizumab risk: PML (JC virus screening required).
B-cell depletion and S1P receptor modulation.

sections.title: Critical Red Flags: Atypical Optic Neuritis
content: Absence of pain (consider NAION or compression).
Severe disc edema with hemorrhages or macular star (Neuroretinitis).
Failure to recover vision after 4-6 weeks.
Bilateral involvement or rapid sequential involvement (Think NMO/MOGAD).
Systemic symptoms (Weight loss, cough, skin lesions).

content.explanation: P: Pulfrich Effect (altered depth perception), H: Hyperacusis, E: Eye Pain (ON), N: Nystagmus (INO), O: Optic Atrophy, M: Marcus Gunn Pupil (RAPD), E: Uhthoff's (Heat sensitivity), N: Neuralgia (Trigeminal), A: Ataxia.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearl: The Pulfrich Effect
content: Occurs due to delayed conduction in the affected optic nerve.
An object moving in a straight line appears to move in an elliptical path.
Can be neutralized by placing a neutral density filter over the fellow (good) eye.
Highly specific for previous optic neuritis.

sections.title: The Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial (ONTT) Key Findings
content: IV Steroids speed up the rate of recovery but do not affect long-term visual outcome (at 1 year).
Low-dose oral steroids (1mg/kg) doubled the risk of recurrence.
Steroids provide a temporary protective effect (2 years) against the development of clinically definite MS.
Baseline MRI is the strongest predictor of MS risk (72% if ≥1 lesion vs 25% if 0 lesions at 15 years).

sections.title: Advanced Diagnostic Workup Flow
content: 1. Neuro-Ophthalmic Exam (RAPD, Color, Visual Fields, Motility).
2. MRI Brain & Orbits with/without Gadolinium (Standard of care).
3. OCT: Quantify RNFL and GCL loss (thinning starts ~3-6 months post-ON).
4. Serology: AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG (rule out NMO/MOGAD if atypical).
5. VEP (Visual Evoked Potentials): Shows prolonged latency in demyelination.
6. Lumbar Puncture: Only if MRI is inconclusive or atypical features present.
